question: Food establishment has an updated FSSAI License & NOC from local authority.
The premises have separate provision for the slaughter of different species of animals & for different methods of slaughter.
There is an adequate resting area (lairage) with facility for watering and examination of animals or birds.
The layout of slaughter house ensures forward movement from live animal introduction to emergence of meat and offals without overlap/intersection.
Internal structure & fittings are made of non-toxic, impermeable materials which prevent entry of dirt, dust & pest.
Floors are impervious, epoxy coated and non-slippery.
Walls are paved with impervious glazed tiles upto 1m for small ruminants/poultry and upto 5m for large animals & epoxy coated.
Windows & other openings are free from accumulated dirt, those which open are fitted with insect-proof screen.
Doors are smooth, non-absorbent surface, close fitted & self closing (where appropriate).
Premises have sufficient lighting i.e. 540 lux (inspection points), 220 lux (work room) & 110 lux (other areas).
Adequate ventilation is provided within the premises.
Personnel hygiene facilities available including toilets, hand washing with warm/hot and cold water, hygienic drying adjacent to toilets and processing entry.
Clean potable cold water (meeting standards of IS 10500) with pressure hose pipes and supply of hot water is available in slaughter hall.
An equipped laboratory is available with qualified chemist/analyst & veterinary microbiologist.
The equipment & containers (except chopping blocks, cutting boards & brooms) are durable, made of corrosion resistant material facilitating cleaning.
Animals suspected of infectious diseases are segregated and kept in separation.
Humane methods are used for slaughtering. Animals rested before slaughter to reduce stress. Not slaughtered in sight of other animals. Stunning done before slaughtering.
Equipment used for stunning is maintained in good working condition.
The dressing of carcasses is not done on floor. Suitable hoists are provided to hang carcasses before evisceration.
Knives and sharpeners (mushtala) are of stainless steel and sterilized/sanitized before use.
All animals are subjected to ante-mortem examination and post-mortem inspection by authorised veterinarian as per specified proforma.
When dressed meat has to stored without further immediate processing, storage is maintained at 0°C to 2°C.
Carcasses/organs fit for consumption marked as Inspected & passed; unfit marked as Inspected & condemned.
Cleaning of equipment, food premises is done per schedule & programme. (Floorings washed daily; lime/colour/paint washing at least once in 12 months).
Preventive maintenance of stunning equipment is carried out regularly per manufacturer instructions.
Blood, manure, garbage, hide, viscera and offals removed within 8 hours after slaughtering without contamination; containers cleaned/disinfected immediately.
Pest control programme is available and pest control activities are carried out by trained and experienced personnel.
No signs of pest activity or infestation in premises (eggs, larvae, faeces etc).
Efficient drainage system; drains/gutters fitted with traps and screens. Blood drainage underground with cleaning facility or portable covered receptacle.
Sufficient space for separation and storage of condemned carcasses. Destruction carried out under direct supervision of authorised veterinarian.
Slaughter house refuse and waste processed into animal by-product or dumped in covered pits.
For large slaughter house, ETP is required. Disposal of sewage and effluents conforms to Environment Protection Act, 1986.
Annual medical examination & inoculation of food handlers against enteric group of diseases per recommended vaccine schedule is done. Check for records.
No person suffering from illness or open wounds/burns involved in handling food or food-contact materials.
Food handlers maintain personal cleanliness (clean clothes, trimmed nails & waterproof bandage) and behaviour (hand washing, no loose jewellery/smoking/spitting).
Food handlers equipped with suitable aprons, gloves, headgear, shoe cover etc.
Internal / External audit of system is done periodically. Check for records.
Food Business has an effective consumer complaints redressal mechanism.
Food handlers have necessary knowledge and skills & trained to handle food safely. Check for training records.
Appropriate documentation & records are available and retained for 1 year or shelf-life of product, whichever is more.
